why: Default is ours loses, and mostly does: benchmark section is schema-only, hand-typed candidate_results, no timer run; loop_audit.py's IO_MARKERS misses .fetchall()/.json()/ORM .all(), measuring nothing radon/scalene would for real. But git-commit+diff-hash state binding, wired into a live pre_push_gate.py hook, is governance none of the 9 alternatives do - they measure, none gates a push on a written comparison. Split: keep gate/schema/provenance; replace loop heuristic with radon/scalene; require benchmark fields from real pytest-benchmark/pyperf JSON via run-check, not hand-typed.

alternatives.name: hypothesis
alternatives.covers: Property-based test generation: creates/shrinks input cases to find edge-case failures automatically.
alternatives.gap: No decision record, no candidate comparison, no git-state binding, no push gate; strengthens an oracle, does not govern or gate a claim.
alternatives.cost: Free, pip install, pure Python, Windows-native.
alternatives.maturity: Very mature, actively maintained core PyPI testing library.

alternatives.name: pytest-benchmark
alternatives.covers: Real statistical timing: calibrated rounds, min/max/mean/stddev, regression compare vs stored baseline JSON.
alternatives.gap: Numbers only; no acceptance-criteria mapping, no candidate rationale, no git-state binding, no push gate.
alternatives.cost: Free, pytest plugin, pip install, Windows-fine.
alternatives.maturity: Active; 5.2.3 released Mar 2026, Tidelift-backed (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: pyperf
alternatives.covers: PSF-maintained low-level benchmark toolkit: process calibration, worker spawns, mean/stddev for microbenchmarks.
alternatives.gap: Timing only, no schema/gate/provenance; Windows worker-spawn behavior not independently verified here.
alternatives.maturity: Active; 2.10 released Feb 2026, PSF org (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: mutmut
alternatives.covers: Mutation testing: injects bugs, checks whether the test suite actually kills them - measures oracle strength ours assumes.
alternatives.gap: No decision record, no push gate; docs require WSL on Windows, violating the 'No WSL dependency' house rule.
alternatives.cost: Free, pip install; Windows path needs WSL per project docs.
alternatives.maturity: Active; 3.3.1 current, maintained by boxed/mutmut (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: radon
alternatives.covers: Computes real cyclomatic complexity and maintainability index by parsing code, not guessing from names.
alternatives.gap: No 'I/O inside loop' semantic flag, no review-question prompts, no git/push integration, no candidate comparison.
alternatives.cost: Free, pip install, pure Python, Windows-fine.
alternatives.maturity: Mature/stable, 4.1.0 current, modest churn (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: vulture
alternatives.gap: Unrelated job; does not flag I/O-in-loop, does not benchmark, does not gate anything.
alternatives.maturity: Mature but quiet; last major release ~2023, still installable and functional.

alternatives.name: scalene
alternatives.covers: Real dynamic CPU/GPU/memory profiler, line-level attribution, shows where time/memory actually goes.
alternatives.gap: No decision/evidence record, no acceptance-criteria mapping, no push gate; a profiler, not a governance layer.
alternatives.cost: Free, pip install; full Windows memory profiling shipped since v2.0 per project issue tracker.
alternatives.maturity: Active; repo updates through May 2026, UMass PLASMA lab project (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: py-spy
alternatives.covers: Sampling profiler attaching to a live process without code changes; officially supports win-64.
alternatives.gap: Pure profiler; no schema, no candidate comparison, no push gate, no acceptance-criteria linkage.
alternatives.cost: Free, pip install, official Windows-64 binary.

alternatives.name: hand-written benchmark (timeit/perf_counter)
alternatives.covers: One real measured number from one real run, zero dependencies, full control of methodology.
alternatives.gap: No repeated-trial statistics unless self-coded, no comparison record, no push gate, no git-state binding.
alternatives.maturity: N/A - a technique, not a maintained package; always available.

migration_loc: Delete loop_audit.py heuristic (~180 lines), add ~50-line radon/scalene wrapper; add ~40 lines ingesting pytest-benchmark/pyperf JSON; new pyproject.toml/uv.lock (~20 lines). Net approx -180/+110.
what_ours_does: implementation_proof.py: JSON schema + ~210-line validator enforcing report completeness, no execution. command_run_check subprocess.run()s a check, sha256-hashes output, capture_repo_state binds pass/fail to a real git commit+diff hash, consumed by a live pre_push_gate.py hook. loop_audit.py: static ast/regex heuristic flagging loops via a 25-word I/O name list; no execution, no metric.
strongest_counterargument: One maintainer, 915 lines, zero third-party deps, already tested (18 passing), already wired into a working push gate. loop_audit.py itself says "review prompts, not proof of a defect" - it never claimed oracle authority. Adding radon/pytest-benchmark/pyperf/scalene is new supply-chain surface for a solo tool whose real job is forcing a written comparison before push, not publishing a benchmark.
